subject: ascendedHero

prompt:
Image 1 is a grey clay maquette of this figure: follow its pose, its parts and its framing, the whole figure from head to foot filling the square as it does, seen three-quarter front from a little above. It is a crude blockout: take its pose, its parts and its framing, not its stubby proportions. Paint over it completely: no grey clay and no plain smooth shapes may remain. Image 2 is a style reference only: match its painting style, brushwork, candle lighting, rim light, muted colours and dark background. Do not copy its head-and-shoulders framing. The subject, its face, its headgear and every ornament must follow the description below exactly; do not copy the man, the helm, the horns, the fur or the trim from Image 2.

A full-length painted portrait of the Ascended Hero, a mortal champion raised to godhood: a lean warrior a head taller than a man, ageless and noble, in a regal pose: standing tall, weight even, chin raised, the sword held upright before the chest in the right hand, the left hand on the belt. Three-quarter front view, the body and the face turned slightly toward the right side of the image. Square image. Framing: the whole figure fills the height of the square: the top of the head about 6% from the top edge and the feet about 94% from the top, centred, with dark empty space around the silhouette. One figure only: no people, no worshippers, no other creatures, no text, no border, no frame, no signature, no logo.
Lighting: a single warm candle key light from the upper left, a dim warm fill, deep warm shadows, and a thin soft warm rim light along the head, the shoulders and the cape that separates the whole silhouette clearly from the background. As in the style reference, much of the figure falls into deep warm shadow: the candle picks out the upper left of the head, the shoulders and the chest, and the lower body and the far side sink into the dark; it is not evenly lit. Background: plain, unpatterned, very dark warm brown close to #1C1A17, with no objects, no landscape, no horizon and no floor: the dark background runs unbroken to the bottom edge, with only a faint soft shadow under the feet.
Medium: painterly oil on a wood panel, loose visible brushwork and soft edges as in the style reference, moderate detail, never a crisp, clean digital illustration; a strong readable silhouette: the shape of the circlet, the long cape and the upright sword against the dark background must still read when the image is shrunk to 64 pixels.
Colors: muted and earthy. The one clear colour of the figure is its long cape: dull ember-orange cloth (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour. All metal is dull old gold (#C9A23E), darkened and worn. Nothing in the image glows. No other saturated area larger than a small clasp or trim.

Subject: Headgear: a simple circlet of dull old gold (#C9A23E), darkened and worn around the brow, no helm; short dark hair. Face: a lean, calm, ageless face of ash-grey skin (#8F8C88), steady eyes. Armour: a coat of dark mail under a fitted breastplate of dark steel trimmed with old gold, plain, with no heraldry and no device; dark leather boots. Mantle: a long cape of dull ember-orange cloth (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour falling from both shoulders to the heels, its edge bordered with a narrow lichen grey-green (#909080) band. Weapon: a straight one-handed sword with a plain straight blade and a gold crossguard. Proportions: tall and heroic, a towering figure with long legs (the legs about half of its height) and the head about one eighth of its height; never squat, stocky, short-legged or dwarf-like.
Paint it as described, the whole figure clearly in view; a little more weathered and ancient in its surfaces, with a heavier, more imposing stance.

Corrections from the previous attempt, which must be fixed: the whole figure must be inside the square: its feet or base about 94% from the top, with dark empty space below them (the previous attempt failed: framing: lowest row 1.0 outside [0.8, 0.995]); the boots were cut by the bottom edge and the sword was held low at the side; the whole figure must stand inside the square with dark space under the boots, and the sword must be held upright before the chest in the right hand, point up, the left hand on the belt.
